description.sr:
Napiši funkciju `createCounter(start = 0)` koja vraća funkciju. Svaki poziv vraćene funkcije povećava brojač za 1 i vraća novu vrednost.

Svaki brojač ima svoje stanje, bez globalnih promenljivih.

Primer:
```js
const c = createCounter();
c(); // 1
c(); // 2
```
description.en:
Write a function `createCounter(start = 0)` that returns a function. Each call of the returned function increases the counter by 1 and returns the new value.

Every counter has its own state, with no global variables.

Example:
```js
const c = createCounter();
c(); // 1
c(); // 2
```

text.sr:
Deklaracija funkcije koja pravi brojač. Svaki poziv `createCounter` vraća novi, nezavisan brojač.

- `function createCounter` pravi funkciju sa imenom `createCounter`. Test je poziva tim imenom.
- `(start = 0)` je parametar sa **podrazumevanom vrednošću**. Ako funkciju pozovemo bez argumenta (`createCounter()`) ili sa `undefined`, `start` je `0`. Ako je pozovemo sa `createCounter(10)`, `start` je `10`.
- Obrati pažnju: samo `undefined` aktivira podrazumevanu vrednost. `createCounter(null)` bi dalo `start = null`.
- `{` otvara telo; zatvara ga `}` u liniji 4.
text.en:
Declaration of the function that creates a counter. Every call of `createCounter` returns a new, independent counter.

- `function createCounter` creates a function named `createCounter`. The test calls it by that name.
- `(start = 0)` is a parameter with a **default value**. If we call the function without an argument (`createCounter()`) or with `undefined`, `start` is `0`. If we call it with `createCounter(10)`, `start` is `10`.
- Note: only `undefined` triggers the default value. `createCounter(null)` would give `start = null`.
- `{` opens the body; it is closed by `}` on line 4.

text.sr:
Pravimo promenljivu `count`: ona čuva trenutnu vrednost brojača.

- `let` pravi promenljivu čija se vrednost može menjati. Mora `let`, jer `const` ne bi dozvolio da je uvećavamo.
- `= start` kopira vrednost parametra `start` u `count`. Brojevi se kopiraju po vrednosti, pa kasnije menjanje `count` ne menja `start`.
- Ova promenljiva pripada ovom jednom pozivu funkcije `createCounter`. Svaki novi poziv pravi svoj, poseban `count`. Zato su brojači nezavisni: uvećanje jednog ne utiče na drugi (skriveni test to proverava).

Dva brojača, dve nezavisne promenljive:

```
const a = createCounter();    // a ima svoj count = 0
const b = createCounter(10);  // b ima svoj count = 10
```
text.en:
We create the variable `count`: it holds the counter's current value.

- `let` creates a variable whose value can change. It has to be `let`, because `const` would not allow us to increase it.
- `= start` copies the value of the parameter `start` into `count`. Numbers are copied by value, so changing `count` later does not change `start`.
- This variable belongs to this one call of `createCounter`. Every new call creates its own, separate `count`. That is why the counters are independent: increasing one does not affect the other (the hidden test checks this).

Two counters, two independent variables:

```
const a = createCounter();    // a has its own count = 0
const b = createCounter(10);  // b has its own count = 10
```

text.sr:
Vraćamo funkciju. To je ono što dobijamo kad pozovemo `createCounter`, i što kasnije zovemo `c()`.

- `return` vraća vrednost, a ta vrednost je ovde funkcija.
- `() => ...` je strelica funkcija bez parametara (prazne zagrade). Desno od strelice je vrednost koju vraća, pa nema posebnog `return` ni vitičastih zagrada.
- To je **closure**: vraćena funkcija i dalje „vidi“ promenljivu `count`, iako je `createCounter` davno završila. Promenljiva ostaje živa dokle god postoji funkcija koja je koristi.
- `++count` je **prefiksno uvećanje**. `++` znači „dodaj 1 na promenljivu“. Dakle `++count` radi dve stvari, tim redom: 1) uveća `count` za 1, 2) vrati NOVU vrednost. Pri svakom pozivu vraćene funkcije `count` raste za još jedan, pa brojač stalno ide: 1, 2, 3...
- Zašto ne `count++`: to je **postfiksno** uvećanje, koje takođe uveća `count` za 1, ali vrati STARU vrednost (onu pre uvećanja). Prvi poziv bi tada dao `0` umesto `1`. To je česta greška.

Tok za `const c = createCounter();` pa tri poziva:

```
pre poziva:      count = 0
c() → ++count:   count postaje 1, vraća 1
c() → ++count:   count postaje 2, vraća 2
c() → ++count:   count postaje 3, vraća 3
```

A sa `count++` bi bilo:

```
c() → count++:   vraća 0 (staru vrednost), pa count postaje 1
c() → count++:   vraća 1, pa count postaje 2
```
text.en:
We return a function. That is what we get when we call `createCounter`, and what we later call as `c()`.

- `return` returns a value, and here that value is a function.
- `() => ...` is an arrow function with no parameters (empty parentheses). To the right of the arrow is the value it returns, so there is no separate `return` or curly braces.
- This is a **closure**: the returned function still “sees” the variable `count` even though `createCounter` finished long ago. The variable stays alive as long as a function that uses it exists.
- `++count` is a **prefix increment**. `++` means “add 1 to the variable”. So `++count` does two things, in this order: 1) it increases `count` by 1, 2) it returns the NEW value. On every call of the returned function `count` grows by one more, so the counter keeps going: 1, 2, 3...
- Why not `count++`: that is the **postfix** increment, which also increases `count` by 1 but returns the OLD value (the one before the increase). The first call would then give `0` instead of `1`. This is a common mistake.

Flow for `const c = createCounter();` followed by three calls:

```
before the call: count = 0
c() → ++count:   count becomes 1, returns 1
c() → ++count:   count becomes 2, returns 2
c() → ++count:   count becomes 3, returns 3
```

And with `count++` it would be:

```
c() → count++:   returns 0 (the old value), then count becomes 1
c() → count++:   returns 1, then count becomes 2
```

text.sr:
Zatvara telo funkcije `createCounter` otvoreno u liniji 1.

- `}` je par za `{`. Svaka otvorena `{` mora da ima svoju `}`; ako jedna fali, JavaScript uopšte ne može da pročita kod (`SyntaxError`).
text.en:
Closes the body of `createCounter` opened on line 1.

- `}` is the pair of `{`. Every opened `{` must have its `}`; if one is missing, JavaScript cannot read the code at all (`SyntaxError`).

note.sr: Vraćena funkcija "pamti" promenljivu `count` iz okruženja u kome je napravljena.
note.en: The returned function "remembers" the `count` variable from the scope it was created in.
